mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or Registrar of Companies in the foreign investor's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Notarize the original certificate by a local notary public in the jurisdiction of origin. 2) If the origin jurisdiction is a contracting state to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille certificate from that state's designated competent authority. 3) If the origin jurisdiction is not an Apostille contracting state, obtain consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate after authentication by the host-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Apostille and Consular Legalization paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially. 4) Obtain a certified Chinese translation before submission to SAMR or its filing agent.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry, Companies House, or equivalent corporate registrar in the foreign jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Obtain the official Certificate of Good Standing from the foreign registry. 2) Have it notarized in the country of origin. 3) If the country participates in the Apostille Convention, apply for a Hague Apostille; if the country does not participate, follow the consular legalization channel through the PRC Embassy or Consulate after host-state Foreign Ministry legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and sequential chaining is strictly prohibited. 4) Prepare a certified Chinese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Execute the Board Resolution and Power of Attorney before a notary public in the foreign investor's jurisdiction. 2) For Apostille Convention states, attach a Hague Apostille from the competent authority; for non-member states, arrange authentication by the host-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by legalization at the PRC Embassy or Consulate. These two routes are distinct and mutually exclusive; no sequential combination is permitted. 3) Provide a notarized or certified Chinese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association, Memorandum of Association, or Charter of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or a notary public authorized to certify constitutive documents in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Obtain a certified copy of the constitutional document from the foreign registry or other competent authority. 2) Notarize the certified copy. 3) Depending on the home jurisdiction, either add a Hague Apostille certificate or initiate consular legalization with the host-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then the PRC Embassy or Consulate. The Apostille and consular routes are mutually exclusive, parallel alternatives and must not be combined. 4) Translate into Chinese by a qualified translator and certify the translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the foreign investor's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the foreign investor's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Request the bank to issue a reference letter on the bank's official letterhead with the authorized signatory's wet-ink signature and bank seal. 2) Notarize the signatory's authority and the document in the country of origin. 3) If the country is an Apostille contracting state, procure a Hague Apostille; if not, proceed through consular legalization at the PRC Embassy or Consulate, after the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Apostille and consular legalization are separate exclusive paths and must not be applied sequentially. 4) Add a certified Chinese translation.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover every UBO, shareholder above 25%, legal representative, director, supervisor, senior manager, authorized signatory, and anyone exercising material control over the WFOE. Screen full names, aliases, nationalities, dates and places of birth, identification document numbers, and ownership chains against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and non-SDN sanctions lists, EU and HM Treasury consolidated financial sanctions lists, PBOC's anti-money laundering blacklist, SAMR's disqualified director database, and Chinese court enforcement and bad-debtor databases. PEP status must be assessed with reference to Chinese domestic prominent public officials, foreign PEPs, and senior international organization officials. Sanctions hits, adverse media, or unexplained PEP exposure must be escalated to the legal and fit-and-proper committee and resolved in writing before any name reservation or incorporation filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration and Reservation Platform, integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A registered Chinese enterprise name must have the statutory four-tier structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and organizational form such as Limited Liability Company. The trade name must use standard Chinese characters. A foreign-investor name used as the trade name must be transliterated phonetically into standard Chinese characters and checked against the SAMR name database; the English name is not a statutory component, but any external English name must be a faithful translation. Registered Chinese names may not contain Roman script, Arabic numerals, or special symbols except as expressly permitted by the enterprise name registration authority. All four tiers are mandatory in the statutory owner-enterprise name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Other false or deceptive superlatives requiring ministerial approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days after receiving a SAMR name rejection notice, the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration application to the market regulation authority at the next higher level, or, where the original authority is the deciding body, to the same authority pursuant to the Regulations on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (2021). The application must attach the rejection notice, a written statement of legal non-conflict, the proposed four-tier name, and a certified translation of any foreign-sourced trade name. The authority is required to issue a written decision within the statutory review period. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent basic People's Court within six months. During the appeal, the applicant may simultaneously prepare a second replacement name for reservation following the same four-tier doctrine.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaged in physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates under ISIC 4661, a pure virtual office, shared desk, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the sole registered address. The municipal tax authority and licensed banks, particularly under high-risk commodity trade AML rules, reject premises that do not show physical possession, business signage, leasehold rights, and operational substance. A residential address is also prohibited. The WFOE must maintain a staffed commercial office in a building with valid property ownership documentation, a lease term of at least one year, current rent invoices, utility bills in the company's name, and the ability to produce written records and personnel on demand. A remote-work arrangement may only be used as a supplementary model after the physical office is fully established and inspected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: commercial property ownership certificate; lease agreement registered with the local housing authority; rent payment vouchers and invoices; utility bills; on-site signage; presence of a legal representative or responsible manager; availability of financial records, corporate chops, bank statements, and tax filing materials; verified absence of residential or PO-box substitution. Quantified risk: high, with an estimated 85% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by municipal tax, SAMR, or state taxation administration officers within the first 12 months of incorporation. For a high-risk energy commodity trading WFOE, the likelihood rises to 95% if VAT anomalies, invoice irregularities, bank suspicious transaction reports, or UBO transparency deficiencies appear. At least one joint inspection by SAMR and local tax authorities should be assumed in the first operating year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised 2023, effective July 1, 2024), principally Articles 23, 24, 27, 35, 46 through 58, 59 through 73, 75, 83 and 84; read together with the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020), Articles 4, 6, 10, 17, 30 and 42; and the Regulations for Implementing the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), as applicable to the establishment, governance, corporate organs and statutory filing obligations of a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company operating in China (Mainland).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal or Provincial Administration for Market Regulation of the jurisdiction where the WFOE's registered office is located, through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the integrated Government Affairs Service Platform; after incorporation, the public-security seal-engraving registration, tax registration, social insurance registration and foreign-exchange registration are separately handled by the Public Security Bureau, the State Taxation Administration, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form (including the Company Registration (Establishment) Application, shareholder information, subscribed capital schedule, Articles of Association, and the Foreign Investment Information Report), filed online or in person with the local Market Supervision Administration; the issuance of the Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code is the definitive statutory incorporation instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The PRC Company Law (2023 Revision) does not impose a minimum paid-up capital or a mandatory blocked escrow account for an ordinary limited-liability WFOE. The Articles of Association must state the subscribed capital and the contribution schedule, and shareholders must contribute their subscribed capital in full within five years after incorporation unless an industry-specific rule or an extended statutory arrangement applies. There is no escrow or blocked-account requirement. For a WFOE engaged in hazardous-chemical or oil-product trading, the licensing authorities may require documented financial capacity and a safety-risk liability arrangement, but no minimum registered capital is mandated. Non-cash contributions, if any, must be appraised and transferred under Article 48 of the PRC Company Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS IN WRITING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INSERT WFOE NAME] LIMITED (THE "COMPANY")

The undersigned, being all of the duly appointed directors of the Company, acting pursuant to Article [•] of the Articles of Association and Article 73 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised 2023), do hereby waive any requirement of notice, meeting, or quorum and adopt the following resolutions as of [DATE]:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the issuance, allotment, and subscription of the registered capital of the Company, in the total amount of [US$ / RMB] [•], divided into [•] equity interests, be and hereby are approved, ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each shareholder shall contribute the subscribed capital in accordance with the contribution schedule set forth in the Articles of Association and the Subscription Agreement, and that the Legal Representative and/or the General Manager, acting jointly or singly as authorized, are hereby authorized to accept capital contributions, issue capital contribution certificates, open the required escrow or ordinary capital cash accounts, and file all capital registration statements with the State Administration for Market Regulation.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and hereby is fixed at [Registered Address], People's Republic of China, and that the Legal Representative be and hereby is authorized to execute, deliver, and register any lease, sublease, service agreement, property ownership confirmation, and related document for such office with the local Administration for Market Regulation and all applicable authorities.

3. BANKING AUTHORITY. RESOLVED, that the Company establish and maintain RMB and foreign-currency bank accounts with [BANK NAME], and that any [one] / [two] of the following authorized signatories, namely [NAME, TITLE] and [NAME, TITLE], acting [alone] / [jointly], be and hereby are authorized to open accounts, sign account-opening forms, issue wire-transfer instructions, execute loan or standby-letter-of-credit arrangements, and approve all disbursements reasonably required for incorporation, licensing, and operations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all formation expenses, government filing fees, notarization and legalization costs, professional fees, and payments for operating licenses are hereby approved.

4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [NAME] be and hereby is appointed as the first Legal Representative and Executive Director of the Company, [NAME] as General Manager, [NAME] as Supervisor, and [NAME] as Company Secretary or Board Secretary, each to hold office until earlier replacement or removal in accordance with the Articles of Association and the Company Law. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each officer is authorized to exercise all powers consistent with the Foreign Investment Law, the Company Law, and the petroleum product wholesale and hazardous-chemical safety regulations, including the preparation and submission of all filings and licensing applications.

5. GENERAL AUTHORITY. RESOLVED, that the Legal Representative and the General Manager, jointly and severally, be and hereby are authorized to negotiate, execute, submit, and do all acts, deeds, certificates, and documents necessary to effect incorporation, corporate governance registrations, tax and foreign-exchange registrations, customs enrollment, hazardous-chemical licensing, environmental approval, and banking operations, and to engage notaries, attorneys, and other professional advisers in connection therewith.

6. EFFECTIVENESS. RESOLVED, that these resolutions take effect immediately and may be signed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) name-reservation portal administered by the local Administration for Market Regulation of the intended registered municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the SAMR online name-reservation system or the local Government Affairs Service Platform and file a proposed Chinese trade name composed of administrative division, trade name, industry or business characteristic, and organization form. For a petroleum-product wholesale WFOE, select a business scope related to energy commodity wholesale and avoid any name elements implying crude oil production or refinery operations, which would trigger additional administrative approvals. Submit the proposed name, the business scope, the intended registered address, and the foreign investor's legal identity. After preliminary checks by the system, the name is reserved for six months; if the name contains restricted words or resembles an existing trademark or enterprise name, the system will issue a rejection.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor's notarized and legalized identity certificate or certificate of incorporation
Proposed Chinese company name (three to five alternative names recommended)
Detailed business scope for wholesale of crude oil, refined fuels, marine fuel oil and related products
Name-reservation application form or online submission record
Power of attorney or authorization letter appointing the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged for similarity, re-file immediately through the same portal using an alternative trade name, distinctive Chinese transliteration, or a different administrative division. Where restricted words are involved, submit a supporting explanation from the relevant industry regulator; if the rejection persists, file an administrative reconsideration or complaint with the higher-level Administration for Market Regulation within five working days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, legalization and preparation of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent notary public in the foreign investor's jurisdiction, PRC Embassy or Consulate (for legalization or apostille), the registered foreign investor, and the intended WFOE shareholders; the final documents will be filed with the local SAMR.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the definitive Articles of Association for the WFOE, which must contain the company name, registered address, business scope, subscribed capital and contribution schedule, shareholders' particulars, board composition, legal representative designation, supervisor, profit distribution rules, liquidation provisions and amendment procedures. Foreign corporate shareholders must have their company registration, incumbency, board resolution and identity documents notarized in the home country and then legalized or apostilled for use in China; individual foreign shareholders must authenticate passport signatures. Secure the registered-office lease with a certified copy of the property ownership certificate and the lessor's identity documents. Execute the first board resolution in writing before or immediately after signing the Articles. These originals will be submitted to the local SAMR in the following step.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized foreign investor corporate registration and beneficial-ownership extracts
Apostilled or consular legalization stamps
Notarized copy of the foreign investor's board resolution approving investment in the WFOE
Signed Articles of Association
Signed pro-forma first board resolution
Letter of appointment of legal representative, general manager, supervisor and secretary
Original or notarized copy of the office lease and property title certificate
Foreign Investment Information Report draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR or the document-review process rejects the notarization, obtain a fresh notarized copy from the original notary or a certified translation by a Chinese translation company and re-legalize if needed. If the lease is defective because the property certificate does not match the lessor, obtain a replacement lease or a notarized confirmation from the property owner. The rehearing or re-filing should be completed within 15 working days before the statutory timeline expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application and issuance of business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System or the local Government Affairs Service Platform counter for foreign-invested enterprise establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form together with the signed Articles of Association, notarized and legalized identity documents, capital contribution schedule, office lease and property certificate, appointment forms for the legal representative and supervisor, and the Foreign Investment Information Report. The application form and constitutional documents must be signed by the investor's authorized representative and, where required, by the proposed legal representative. SAMR will review the name, business scope, registered capital, organizational structure, registered address and compliance with foreign-investment negative-list restrictions. Upon acceptance, SAMR issues the Business License with the Unified Social Credit Code, confirming the effective date of incorporation and the legal person status of the WFOE.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Notarized and legalized investor identity certificates
Foreign Investment Information Report
Registered-office lease and property certificate
Appointment documents for legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager
Pro-forma first board resolution
Consent of the landlord and non-foreign-investment negative-list declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a rectification notice, answer the specific query within 15 working days by submitting corrected signatures, additional notarized translations or an amended Articles of Association. If the business scope is suspended because a special license is required, apply for the Hazardous Chemical Business License concurrently and request a conditional registration where law permits. If the application is rejected, appeal or re-file after correcting all grounds; the re-filed application is treated as a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company seal engraving and public security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) authorized seal-engraving service providers; the engraving is notified to the local Public Security Bureau for filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Business License, procure the company seal, financial seal, legal-representative name seal, contract seal, and customs seal if import/export is intended. Authorized seal-engraving workshops must register the seal impressions with the Public Security Bureau and provide a Seal Filing Certificate or Seal Registration Record. The legal representative, or a person holding a notarized power of attorney, must appear with the original Business License and unified social credit code certificate. The contract seal and bank-document seal are essential for opening the corporate bank account, executing standby letters of credit, and filing the hazardous-chemical license application. The seals must be kept under dual custody as required by the company's internal control policies.
required_dossiers: Original Business License
Legal representative identity certificate
Power of attorney and agent identity certificate, if applicable
Application form for seal engraving and filing
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Approval or record of establishment registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal-engraving service refuses to issue the seal because of missing legal-representative biometric data, arrange for the legal representative to attend the workshop or the PSB acceptance point in person. If the seal registration is delayed, obtain a written receipt from the PSB and use that receipt for tax and license applications. If a seal is lost, file a police loss report, publish the loss statement in a designated newspaper and re-engrave under an updated filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, bank account opening, foreign exchange registration and social insurance enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (local Tax Service Bureau), commercial bank, State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated bank, and local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Under the multi-license reform, tax registration may be completed automatically after the Business License is issued, but the WFOE must complete tax payer qualification, select the accounting system, and submit an electronic invoice quota application. Open a basic deposit account with a commercial bank and a foreign exchange capital account if foreign-direct-investment capital will be injected, and then complete SAFE foreign-exchange registration for the WFOE through the bank. For import or export of petroleum products, complete Customs enrollment and obtain the Customs Registration Record. Register the employer with social insurance, medical insurance and housing-fund authorities. Failure to register within 30 days for tax and within the prescribed period for SAFE may trigger administrative penalties.
required_dossiers: Business License
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Articles of Association
Legal representative identity certificate
Company seal, financial seal, and contract seal
Office lease or ownership certificate
Bank account opening application and resolution
Foreign Investment Information Report and SAFE registration forms
Tax registration forms and accounting-system set-up statement
Social insurance and housing-fund registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE challenges the beneficial-ownership information, submit a detailed ownership chain and certification for each ultimate beneficial owner. If tax registration is flawed because the legal representative has not completed face-to-face verification, schedule a tax-bureau biometric appointment and file a written explanation. If social-insurance enrollment is delayed, execute retroactive enrollment and pay all accrued contributions to avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hazardous-chemical operation license and environmental/fire-approval dossier submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial or Municipal Emergency Management Bureau for the Hazardous Chemical Business License; local Ecology and Environment Bureau for the Environmental Impact Assessment and pollution-discharge permit; Fire and Rescue Brigade for fire-protection review and acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the WFOE will take title to, store, wholesale, or physically distribute crude oil, marine fuel oil, or refined products listed as hazardous chemicals, the Hazardous Chemical Business License is a prerequisite to business commencement. Prepare the license application with a safety-production responsibility system, safety management rules, an emergency response plan filed with the Emergency Management Bureau, and a qualified safety-assessment report covering the storage and transshipment premises. If construction or modification of storage facilities is involved, complete the environmental impact assessment procedure and fire-protection design review before construction. For office-only brokerage without physical storage, the EIA is generally not applicable, but the owner of any tank farm or warehouse must satisfy the full regulatory tier. Submit the dossier online or at the government-service window; the authority may conduct a site inspection.
required_dossiers: Hazardous Chemical Business License application form
Safety-production responsibility system and accident-prevention rules
Safety assessment report for the storage or trading facility
Emergency response plan and its filing record
Fire-protection design review and acceptance documents
Environmental impact assessment approval, registration or exemption certificate
Pollution-discharge permit registration or permit, if triggered
Qualified personnel certificates for safety managers and handlers
Site layout, plot plan, process flow, and tank-farm specifications
Certificate of land-use and building ownership or lease for the storage site
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Emergency Management Bureau issues an objection, remedy the safety deficiencies, update the safety assessment, and re-submit the corrected dossier within the statutory response period. If the fire-protection acceptance is denied, initiate structural or fire-resistance upgrades and request a re-inspection after completion. If an environmental classification upgrade requires a full environmental impact report instead of a registration form, commission a qualified EIA unit, conduct public participation and submit the report to the Ecology and Environment Bureau for review before proceeding.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Provincial or Municipal Emergency Management Bureau (Hazardous Chemical Business License); Fire and Rescue Brigade (fire-protection review and acceptance); local Ecology and Environment Bureau (environmental impact assessment and pollution-discharge permit); Ministry of Commerce and National Development and Reform Commission (for crude oil and oil-product import quotas or automatic import licensing, if the WFOE imports energy commodities); General Administration of Customs (customs enrollment and commodity inspection coordination)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Hazardous Chemical Business License issued under the Regulations on the Safety Management of Hazardous Chemicals and the Measures for the Administration of Hazardous Chemical Business Licenses; where the WFOE owns or operates oil or refined-product storage tanks, an additional Storage Facility Safety Approval and Fire Protection Acceptance Certificate; if imports are made, a Crude Oil Non-State Trade Import Authorization or an Automatic Import License for refined oil products, as applicable. For domestic wholesale of refined oil after the 2020 administrative streamlining, a separate Ministry of Commerce refined-oil wholesale qualification is no longer issued; the effective legal gatekeeper is the Hazardous Chemical Business License.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China, with project-specific review by the provincial, municipal or county-level Ecology and Environment Bureau according to the project nature and storage capacity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional. If the WFOE conducts only office-based wholesale brokerage with no physical tank farm, warehouse, process unit, or handling installation, the project-level environmental impact assessment is Not Applicable. If the WFOE constructs or leases an oil or refined-product storage depot, the EIA is classified under the Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment of Construction Projects. As a general control threshold, an oil depot with total storage capacity of 10,000 cubic metres or above requires a Full Environmental Impact Report; storage capacity between 1,000 and 10,000 cubic metres requires an Environmental Impact Report Form; storage capacity below 1,000 cubic metres may require only an Environmental Impact Registration Form, subject to local provincial amendments and sensitive-area factors. No construction may commence before the EIA approval document or completed registration is issued, and after commissioning the operator must obtain or register a Pollution Discharge Permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: direct discharge from tank-farm areas, oil-water separators, equipment washing and stormwater runoff must meet the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard GB 8978-1996, Grade I limits, including petroleum pollutants not exceeding 5 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 100 mg/L, ammonia nitrogen not exceeding 15 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 70 mg/L; if routed to a municipal sewer, the pretreatment limits under GB/T 31962-2015 apply, ordinarily chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 500 mg/L and petroleum pollutants not exceeding 15 mg/L unless a stricter local standard is enacted. Volatile organic compounds: storage tanks, loading arms, flanges, pumps and valves must comply with the national petroleum-storage and transport emission standards (GB 20950 series), the enterprise boundary total non-methane hydrocarbon concentration must not exceed 4.0 mg/m3 on a one-hour average under GB 16297-1996, and an equipment leakage detection and repair (LDAR) program must be implemented with leak-rate intervention thresholds consistent with the applicable technical specifications. Hazardous waste: tank bottom sludge, spent absorbents, oily waste, contaminated filters and wastewater-treatment residue are identified under hazardous-waste category HW08; on-site storage shall comply with GB 18597-2023, shall not exceed one year without a regulatory extension, and must be transferred under a hazardous-waste manifest to a licensed disposal facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire-safety certification for hazardous-chemical storage and transshipment facilities. Before construction, submit the design documents to the Fire and Rescue Brigade for fire-protection design review; after completion, undergo on-site fire-protection acceptance inspection and obtain the fire-protection acceptance certificate before commencing use. The facility must install explosion-proof electrical equipment, lightning and static-protection earthing systems, gas and low-explosion-limit detectors, emergency shut-off and fire-suppression systems, and maintain routine fire-safety inspections. Under the Work Safety Law and the Occupational Disease Prevention and Control Law, the WFOE must conduct an occupational-hazard risk assessment, provide measurement and monitoring of toxic and flammable atmospheres, complete worker occupational-health examinations, and register any major hazard installation with the Emergency Management Bureau if hazardous-chemical quantities exceed the major-hazard threshold. If the building area or land-use type triggers obligations under the People's Air Defense Law, the project must obtain civil-defense (air-raid shelter) construction exemption or construction approval from the local civil-defense office; where civil-defense clearance is not required, an official written exemption notice should be obtained and retained in the compliance file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); electronic portal: E-Tax Platform of the State Taxation Administration (web-based national electronic tax bureau system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must first complete company incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which functions as the legal TIN. Next, within 30 days of obtaining the business license, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the competent local branch of the STA by filing the Information Registration Form for Taxpayers. In the E-Tax platform, the legal representative or authorized tax agent, using the entity's electronic business license, must submit the incorporation certificate, articles of association, lease or proof of business premises, and legal representative identification to obtain the taxpayer registration confirmation and ongoing access to the E-Tax terminal. For direct tax registration of a non-resident entity without a fixed establishment, the non-resident applies for a separate Business Number / non-resident tax registration code via the withholding agent's E-Tax filing, submitting the certificate of incorporation issued by its home jurisdiction, passport or corporate identity evidence, and a completed Application Form for Tax Registration of Non-Resident Enterprises. The E-Tax system then auto-generates the dedicated tax identification numbers for income tax, VAT, and other levy filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification; a WFOE is mandatorily treated as a resident enterprise for corporate income tax purposes if incorporated in mainland China. China has no check-the-box or hybrid entity election. Qualifying offshore-derived income of resident enterprises may separately elect to claim Chinese treaty benefits or the Foreign Tax Credit, but this is not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for corporate entities; all businesses selling goods or services in mainland China must register for VAT upon establishment, regardless of turnover. Small-scale taxpayers with continuous taxable sales below RMB 5,000,000 per year may elect simplified VAT treatment, but registration as a VAT taxpayer is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a national Electronic Invoice (E-Invoice) system and a full digital invoice pilot under the Digital Electronic Invoice (全电发票) programme, rolled out through the E-Tax platform. All VAT taxpayers must issue legally compliant invoices (ordinary or special VAT invoices) through the E-Tax platform or certified third-party electronic invoice systems connected via real-time API to the STA. Special VAT invoices for input VAT credit require the completion of the stapled invoice verification/clearance process where the invoice data is transmitted to STA for authentication and matching before the purchaser may claim a deduction. Goods subject to export or wholesale of refined oil products additionally require the integrated issuance of special VAT invoices with quantity and unit tracking; refined oil product wholesale is subject to enhanced e-invoice monitoring, requiring the invoice to include commodity category, measurement unit, and quantity, and any invoice exceeding normal business volumes triggers automatic fiscal risk flags. The anti-fraud digital stamping requires generation of a unique electronic invoice code, watermark, and cryptography-based QR verification on every VAT invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods, including physical wholesale supplies of marine fuel oil and refined petroleum distillates sold to a non-resident overseas buyer and physically transported out of Chinese customs territory, are zero-rated. The WFOE must obtain an export customs declaration (出口货物报关单) showing the WFOE as the exporter, provide a genuine offshore purchase contract with the foreign buyer, issue a VAT special invoice for export sales, and demonstrate that foreign exchange has been received from the overseas buyer. For fuel sold as stores to international shipping vessels, zero-rating applies where the supply is treated as an export of goods to an international transportation operation, subject to China Customs supervision, bunkering under customs control, and issuance of an export-verification document for bonded/export fuel. Direct cross-border supply of qualifying services is also zero-rated if performed for overseas recipients and consumed offshore, but wholesale commodity brokerage remains governed by goods export rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) with customs assignment number and export customs seal
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal transport document showing port of loading in mainland China and port of discharge outside mainland China
Bunkering or marine fuel supply delivery receipt (for international shipping stores)
Sales contract or purchase order with the overseas non-resident buyer
Customs supervision warehouse / bonded zone outbound transfer voucher, where applicable
Marine fuel export licence or refined oil wholesale licence confirmation, where required
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign exchange receipt confirmation evidencing overseas payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exporters claiming zero-rating or export VAT refund are subject to STA audit and customs data matching. If a zero-rating claim is fraudulent or unverified, the taxpayer must repay the VAT refund or exempted output VAT, is denied input VAT credit, and may be subject to a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on the unpaid/recovered tax and an administrative penalty of up to 50% of the tax involved for failure to truthfully declare. Where fraud is deliberate, the penalty increases to 50%-5x of the unpaid tax, criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law can attach for export tax fraud, and the tax authority may apply a rigorous retroactive clawback for up to 10 years' prior export refund periods if the exporter is found to have engaged in fabricated export documents, false customs declarations, circular or phantom foreign exchange receipts, or under-declared fuel quantities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) via the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current-account convertibility for goods, services, and profit remittance in alignment with IMF Article VIII, but every transaction must be routed through regulated bank channels and is subject to substantive documentary review. The capital account, including foreign direct investment, external debt and portfolio investment, remains controlled and is liberalised only for clearly framed direct investment structures. A WFOE's registered capital injection must be filed under the FDI foreign-exchange registration system, while outward dividend remittance is classified as a current-account item but requires audited financial statements, a board resolution and a tax clearance certificate. The mandatory surrender of export proceeds was abolished in 2012 under SAFE rules; exporters may retain all foreign currency earnings in an eligible foreign-exchange account. Nevertheless, every export receipt must be reported to the Trade Monitoring System within five business days, and the receipt must be linked to the corresponding customs declaration within a matching cycle. For a crude-oil and refined-products broker, offshore re-invoicing and round-trip trading structures are intensely scrutinised because false trade is a classic laundering evading mechanism. Shanghai Free-Trade Zone FT accounts can provide enhanced liquidity, but a standard non-zone domestic WFOE must operate with a regular domestic foreign-exchange account. Overall, the regime is convertible for all genuine transactions but not a free market; every conversion requires the bank to verify the underlying commercial reality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory surrender ratio exists in mainland China; the 2012 repeal of forced settlement allows a WFOE to retain one hundred percent of export proceeds in a designated foreign-currency current account for an unlimited duration. However, all receipts must be declared by the bank into the trade monitoring system within five working days of clearing. The related export declaration must be matched and closed within a reasonable cycle; in practice a matching period of thirty calendar days is routine, extendable to ninety days for large crude or petroleum lots with prior SAFE registration. For transit trade, the receipt must be paired with the corresponding import and export contracts and transport documents; if no matching is completed within forty days, the bank records the item as an unmatched receipt and may restrict subsequent transaction volumes until explanation and rectification. There is no required conversion percentage; all conversions to CNY are discretionary at the market rate. Any single conversion above USD 100,000 equivalent is automatically screened for unusual patterns. Dividend-related conversions must derive from the audited profit certificate and cannot be mislabelled as export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account for FDI settlement and operating foreign-currency account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic RMB deposit account with USD trade settlement sub-account
Commodity trade settlement account covering current and capital transactions
Shipping and energy trading settlement account, supporting standby letters of credit

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal viability; not recommended. The People's Republic of China does not recognise offshore e-money institutions (EMIs) as banks, and a domestic WFOE may not legally hold corporate deposits, open foreign-exchange accounts, or settle commercial trade transactions through an EMI. All cross-border settlement in RMB or foreign currency must be executed by a PRC-licensed commercial bank that is a member of SWIFT and CNAPS. Some EMIs provide front-end digital interfaces backed by a licensed bank, but the account remains with the licensed bank and the full KYC of that bank applies. For a high-risk ISIC 4661 oil-brokerage entity, any attempt to use an EMI-only channel would generate a suspicious transaction report and would be treated by SAFE as operating an illegal foreign-exchange agency. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must be built exclusively on tier-1 domestic bank relationships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PRC bank AML/KYC rules require that a statutory director, or a very senior executive named in a board resolution, appear physically at the opening branch for an in-person interview and biometric verification. Remote-only video KYC is not accepted for high-risk corporates. A non-resident director may appoint an authorised agent under a power of attorney notarised and legalised by the PRC embassy or consulate, but the director must still join a live video call with the bank signing session. The bank will conduct a site visit to the registered office, and for energy trading it will also inspect the physical desk and operating records. Original company seals, including the official chop, financial chop and legal representative chop, must be present. Electronic seals cannot replace the physical chop for the initial opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by layered non-resident holding vehicles, possible nominee shareholding and incomplete UBO information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a notarised UBO register listing every intermediate and ultimate natural person with shareholding percentages and voting rights; certified copies of passports or national IDs for each ultimate controller; certified constitution and share register of the offshore parent; audited or management accounts for the direct parent and the WFOE; a control-chain diagram displaying all layers; written confirmation that no bearer shares or nominee arrangements are used, or if used, the nominee deed plus the beneficiary declaration; and tax-residence certificates to evidence commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags from open-account oil brokerage, including possible phantom cargoes, third-party receiving vessels, and over- or under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete trade package for each transaction: original sales and purchase contracts with Incoterms and price formula; original negotiable bills of lading or independent terminal warehouse receipts; vessel name, IMO, and port-call records; independent inspection certificates from an internationally recognised surveyor such as SGS or Intertek; customs declarations for any cargo crossing China borders; an exact mapping of the payment flow to the transport document; and a certified statement that no receivables are used for off-balance-sheet funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP exposure because energy counterparties may be national oil companies, state-owned trading houses, or persons connected to sanctioned states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver name-screening reports covering all parties, including sub-brokers, shipowners and end users, against the OFAC, European Union, United Nations, UK and China sanctions lists; PEP self-certifications and source-of-wealth statements for any PEP-related UBO; a written compliance undertaking from the appointed AML officer that no sanctioned entity or jurisdiction is involved; and if a sanctioned nexus is identified, provide a legal opinion from a PRC law firm and any necessary PBOC/SAFE approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed or thinly capitalised WFOE in a sector characterised by invoice financing, commodity financing fraud and round-tripping transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish a certified capital verification report from a PRC CPA confirming full payment of registered capital; provide executed framework agreements or term sheets with at least two reputable international counterparties; present credentials and employment contracts of the trading team; submit a detailed 18-month cash flow and banker's advance projection; commit to monthly transaction reconciliations and to a bank covenant permitting annual joint site inspections; optionally add a parent guarantee or standby credit facility from a top-tier bank as additional credit enhancement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Registered capital in USD or another permitted currency must first be recorded through FDI foreign-exchange registration. The WFOE will hold a capital-account foreign deposit account. The incoming SWIFT payment is classified under purpose code '227010' (Foreign Direct Investment Capital Injection). After receipt, the funds may be converted to RMB at the settlement rate and placed in a Renminbi payments account, subject to the capital account payment control review. Disbursement is allowed only for enumerated operating purposes — salaries, rent, freight, inventory, and taxes. The bank will require the underlying board resolution, the share subscription agreement, and a pro-forma invoice where advance payments are requested. A PRC CPA issues a capital verification report based on the credit advice and bank statement. All relevant business registry updates and the annual investment information report are filed with the Market Regulation Administration. Each disbursement above the bank's reporting threshold is submitted to SAFE through the capital account information system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The WFOE will use SWIFT MT103 for prompt payments of bunker fuel and refined-product invoices, each individually supported by a purchase contract and commercial invoice. International imports will be handled by irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued by the domestic bank under UCP600, usually with 30 to 90 day usance, in favour of the upstream refinery or trading house. For spot purchases, a documentary collection (D/P or D/A) may be used. For China-bound crude and product shipments, the bank must see the original bill of lading, insurance certificate, inspection report, and the import licence. For transit or merchanting trade, both legs of the contract, the transport evidence and any storage documents are reviewed before payment release. The outward payment is submitted with purpose code '110' (Goods Trade) and is automatically checked against customs data. If a counterparty is considered higher-risk, the bank may require a standby letter of credit from the same tier-1 bank or a guarantee from another major bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts, known as forward settlement and sale in the domestic market, are permissible for hedging genuine trade and balance-sheet currency exposure; the hedge must be supported by a written real-demand certificate and an existing or reasonably forecast underlying transaction, while speculative forward entry is prohibited.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not allowed onshore for a Chinese-resident WFOE. An NDF can only be executed offshore by the non-resident parent or an affiliated offshore entity, provided the offshore entity has actual USD funding and the onshore WFOE does not receive or settle the CNY difference in a manner that violates SAFE rules.

Cross-currency swaps are permitted for longer-term foreign exchange exposures such as FDI capital accounts or trade finance loans, subject to the notional amount not exceeding the underlying principal and to the bank's product eligibility confirmation.
FX options may be used for hedging actual exposure; exotic option structures with embedded leverage are generally not offered to non-systemic commercial entities.
All hedge transactions must be documented under an ISDA master agreement or the bank's standard local form and must be included in the company's quarterly treasury compliance reporting to the bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Reconciliation Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration / local in-charge tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year following the tax year (calendar year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to RMB 2,000 (RMB 10,000 for serious cases), daily surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax from the due date, enforced collection measures, credit downgrade, and potential administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June each year, covering the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; after three consecutive years of non-reporting, administrative revocation of business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Direct Investment Equity Information Report (FDI Equity Registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) via Capital Project Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June each year, with data as at 31 December of the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of foreign exchange settlement, purchase, and capital account transactions; inclusion in SAFE monitoring list; possible administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce / SAMR jointly through National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Order to rectify within a specified period; fines up to RMB 500,000 for submission of false or misleading information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Annual Report (applicable where import/export registration is active)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of AEO and expedited clearance benefits; downgrade of customs credit rating; possible fines under Customs Law for inaccurate or incomplete reporting.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For this single-shareholder WFOE, the PRC Company Law (Article 62 in the 2018 revision; corresponding provision in the 2023 revision) makes an independent certified CPA audit compulsory irrespective of size. Additional statutory audit triggers under Chinese norms for other limited-company situations are: (a) balance-sheet total assets exceeding RMB 50 million (approximately USD 7.0 million); (b) annual operating turnover exceeding RMB 100 million (approximately USD 14.0 million); (c) 200 or more employees; (d) license-based requirements for energy wholesale trading or financial services; (e) listed or public-interest entity status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards (CAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance; for small entities the Small Business Accounting Standards may apply, but this energy wholesale WFOE uses full CAS, which is substantially converged with IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under PRC regulatory practice, a separate annual UBO confirmation does not exist. Instead, a 30-day event-driven filing obligation applies to any equity transfer, change in ultimate beneficial controller, or change of directors/supervisors, filed with the local SAMR. The annual corporate report (due by 30 June) re-confirms the shareholder and management list, and under anti-money laundering rules applicable to high-risk wholesale energy traders, beneficial ownership information must be refreshed at least annually and before high-risk transactions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages (if any security interest created)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General headline rate is 25%. A preferential 15% rate is available for qualifying New and High-Tech Enterprises; small and low-profit enterprises may benefit from reduced effective rates on taxable income within statutory caps; eligible R&D expenses qualify for a 100% additional deduction; accelerated depreciation is available for certain energy-efficiency, environmental-protection and digital-intelligent production assets. No automatic patent-box or free-zone tax holiday applies to wholesale commodity trading of marine fuel oil and refined petroleum products.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (A Class) — Form A100000, 'Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (A Class)', together with supporting schedules (A105000, A105050, A105080, A107012, A107041 and the transfer pricing disclosure schedules), filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (eTax@China).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional enterprise income tax returns are separately due under Article 54 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual enterprise income tax return must be filed within five months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., May 31 for a calendar-year company, and any balance of tax must be paid by the same date. Quarterly provisional returns must be filed and provisional tax paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from wholesale trading of marine fuel oil, crude oil and refined petroleum products, including brokerage commission, storage, handling and ancillary charges, net of VAT, trade discounts and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the revenue of the Chinese WFOE. If the WFOE acts as agent or broker for a non-resident principal, report the commission or fee income, not the full commodity gross value, unless title, risk and commercial substance pass through the WFOE. Back-to-back trading with an offshore affiliate must be disclosed to avoid transfer-pricing recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold for purchased marine fuel oil, crude oil and refined distillates, including product cost, freight, insurance, storage, inspection and throughput fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter cost at the arm's-length price for intercompany purchases. If a non-resident affiliate supplies product at a price above the comparable market price, make a transfer-pricing add-back adjustment. Do not deduct non-resident group charges absent a valid intercompany service agreement, actual services and supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, administrative expenses and financial expenses, including royalties, management fees, bank charges, interest expense, foreign exchange losses and commission paid to third-party brokers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to non-resident intellectual property owners are deductible only if the technology is genuinely used, the amount is arm's length, and withholding tax has been paid. Interest paid to non-resident related-party lenders is subject to the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalization rule. Management fees or headquarters charges without demonstrable in-China benefit are non-deductible and must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit before tax prepared in accordance with PRC Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reconcile with the audited financial statements. For a WFOE engaged in commodity trading, any consolidated group profit allocated to an offshore related party while the WFOE reports a loss must be supported by a contemporaneous transfer-pricing benchmark prepared before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment items: add-back of non-deductible expenses, transfer-pricing adjustments, disallowed related-party charges, business entertainment limitation, thin-capitalization interest and other permanent/temporary differences; deduction side includes R&D super deduction, dividends from resident investee companies and qualifying loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any royalty, interest or service fee paid to a non-resident where the beneficial owner is not substantiated or treaty documentation is incomplete. Do not deduct dividends distributed or deemed distributed to the foreign parent. Loss carryforwards are limited to five years from the loss year and require prior-year filed returns and substantiation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all tax adjustments, loss carryforwards and special reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the final basis for the 25% headline CIT. If taxable income is zero or negative, the WFOE must still maintain local file and master file documentation if related-party transaction thresholds are exceeded. Non-resident owners cannot use WFOE losses to reduce tax in their own jurisdictions, and China does not permit group loss relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable enterprise income tax rate and the calculated income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% unless a 15% preferential rate certificate has been approved for high-tech status. The tax rate applied to the WFOE's taxable income is unrelated to the 10% withholding tax separately imposed on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit for income taxes lawfully paid abroad on foreign-source income of the Chinese WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only for foreign income tax actually borne by the WFOE on its own foreign-source income, supported by foreign tax certificates. Foreign withholding taxes imposed on the non-resident parent at the time of dividend remittance are not creditable against the WFOE's CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net enterprise income tax payable or refund due after deducting quarterly provisional payments, tax credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle any underpayment by May 31. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05%. When remitting a dividend to the non-resident shareholder, the WFOE must make a separate withholding tax filing and payment; that dividend withholding tax is not reported as part of the WFOE's own CIT liability on Form A100000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 under Article 62 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law. Late payment surcharge: 0.05% per day. False or fraudulent filing under Article 63 attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax plus criminal referral if the evaded tax exceeds the criminal threshold (RMB 50,000 and 10% of statutory tax payable). Failure by a withholding agent to withhold non-resident tax may result in a penalty of 50% to 300% of the un-withheld tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China, under Article 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the detailed rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced treaty rate (commonly 5% for a parent company owning at least 25% of the Chinese WFOE and satisfying beneficial ownership), the non-resident shareholder must provide: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the tax authority of its residence jurisdiction; (ii) a completed treaty benefit application in the form required by the Chinese withholding agent or local tax bureau; (iii) a beneficial ownership declaration with corporate ownership chart, financial substance evidence and a statement that the shareholder is not a conduit; and (iv) evidence of the applicable shareholding period if the DTA provides a minimum holding period. The WFOE, as withholding agent, must submit the withholding return and treaty documentation to the State Taxation Administration before remittance to obtain reduced-rate clearance or must withhold at 10% and allow the non-resident to apply for a tax treaty refund within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10% each. Under China's double taxation agreements, the reduced treaty rate typically ranges from 5% to 10% for royalties and from 7% to 10% for interest depending on the treaty partner and the recipient's beneficial ownership. Royalties or interest effectively connected with a permanent establishment in China are taxable as business profits at the ordinary 25% CIT rate, not as gross-basis withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local file (contemporaneous documentation) is required when annual related-party transactions exceed: RMB 400 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, or RMB 200 million for related-party services. Master file is required when aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion or when the enterprise has revenue above RMB 1 billion and related-party transaction benchmarks exceed the specified thresholds. Annual related-party transaction disclosure schedules must be filed with the annual corporate income tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute in the same manner as certain offshore hubs, but CIT Law Article 47 and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules require that arrangements have a bona fide business purpose and economic substance. A commodity-trading WFOE must demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in China such as active contract negotiation, physical inventory control, shipping and logistics coordination, commodity risk management, treasury decisions and employment of qualified staff. Absent substance, the tax authority may recharacterize the WFOE as a conduit, deny treaty benefits, impose special tax adjustments and levy interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Official Invoice Issuance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately underreports wholesale turnover of crude oil or refined marine fuel products, issues or procures false VAT special invoices for fictitious storage, logistics or consulting services, and shifts taxable profit to offshore related parties through non-arm's-length intercompany purchase prices without contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Article 63 and PRC Criminal Law Article 201 and Article 205. The tax authority may recover the underpaid tax plus 0.05% daily late-payment surcharge and impose a civil penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Issuance or use of false VAT special invoices is a criminal offense punishable by fixed-term imprisonment and criminal fines; the company may be blacklisted, its VAT invoice quota cancelled and its export or customs clearance privileges suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who approves, signs or directs the filing of false returns or false invoices may have the corporate veil pierced under PRC Company Law Article 20, becoming jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid taxes and penalties. The director may also face criminal detention, property preservation, a court-imposed exit ban (travel restriction preventing departure from China), professional disqualification, and imprisonment of up to life imprisonment in aggravated false-invoice cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell Entity / Lack of Economic Substance and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is formally registered with bank accounts and a local board but has no physical business premises, no full-time employees, no genuine inventory management or risk function, and no real decision-making capacity. It is used as a conduit for channeling commodity trading profits to a low-tax offshore parent and to claim tax treaty benefits on outbound dividends, interest or royalties without performing any Core Income-Generating Activities in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Special Tax Adjustment Measures under CIT Law Article 47 and the Tax Administration and Collection Law Article 36. The tax authority may recharacterize the arrangement, disregard the corporate form, adjust taxable income upward, impose interest at an elevated rate for special tax adjustments, deny treaty benefits and impose penalties of up to RMB 200,000 for failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign substance-free intercompany agreements and authorize circular fund flows may be held personally liable under Company Law Article 20 because the corporate veil exists only where bona fide substance exists. The legal representative and responsible directors may be placed on exit restriction lists, their personal assets may be seized to satisfy the adjusted tax and interest, and they may face criminal liability if the shell structure is used to obtain illegal VAT refunds, export rebates or foreign exchange benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade-Based Money Laundering and Sanctions Evasion in Energy Commodity Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE executes cross-border wire payments and standby letters of credit for marine fuel oil and refined products through multiple unregulated intermediaries, uses duplicate or inflated bills of lading for the same cargo, misstates customs value, fails to conduct AML-KYC and beneficial ownership verification on counterparties, or routes product and payments to jurisdictions subject to international sanctions with false end-user certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law Article 48 and Criminal Law Article 191. Institutions may be fined up to RMB 5 million and responsible persons up to RMB 1 million; the AML license or business registration may be revoked. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange may impose fines of 0.5% to 5% of the illegal foreign exchange amount. Customs authorities may confiscate the goods and impose penalties for false customs declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct or approve these illicit payment structures cannot hide behind the WFOE's limited liability. They face personal civil asset restitution, bank account freezes, travel bans and exit restrictions, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution for money laundering carrying up to ten years' imprisonment. If the conduct violates foreign sanctions or anti-money laundering statutes, directors may also face cross-border asset forfeiture actions, extradition proceedings and INTERPOL red notice exposure.
